articles.title: Ensure smooth flow at boundary checkpoints: CS
articles.excerpt: Chief Secretary Eric Chan on Sunday instructed government departments to ensure the smooth flow of travellers at boundary control points. His comments come after footage circulated on social media showing what appeared to be long queues at the checkpoint of mostly seven seaters…
articles.fullText:
Chief Secretary Eric Chan on Sunday instructed government departments to ensure the smooth flow of travellers at boundary control points.

His comments come after footage circulated on social media showing what appeared to be long queues at the checkpoint of mostly seven seaters waiting to cross into Shenzhen after midnight.

The tailback stretched all the way to San Tin Highway at one point.

Large numbers of northbound travellers were also stuck in urban areas, with dozens of people lining up for cross-border coach services in Mong Kok.

Many of them had come to Hong Kong for Halloween festivities or a concert in Kai Tak.

Hong Kong Non-Franchised Bus Association chairman Eddie Choi explained that private cars with permits for other checkpoints all diverted to Huanggang after midnight, since it is the only 24-hour crossing to Shenzhen.

Timothy Chui, executive director of the Hong Kong Tourism Association, said there could be even more cross-border revellers next weekend.

He suggested creating dedicated lanes for buses and coaches around the port facility.

Writing on Facebook, Chief Secretary Eric Chan said he paid a visit to the Shenzhen Bay and Huanggang control points following a visit to Dongguan.

Chan said he directed the Security Bureau to continue ensuring that port operations remain safe, efficient, and orderly.

Authorities were told to proactively assess and forecast passenger traffic, and open additional inspection counters and vehicle lanes ahead of peak periods.

Chan also encouraged travellers to consider staying overnight in the SAR for a more comfortable and fulfilling experience.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: John Catlin wins HK golf open in dominant fashion
articles.excerpt: John Catlin of the United States on Sunday claimed victory at the Hong Kong Open, winning at the iconic Fanling golf course for the seventh Asian Tour trophy of his career. The California native carded a sizzling six-under-par 64 in round four to finish 20-under overall, holding…
articles.fullText:
John Catlin of the United States on Sunday claimed victory at the Hong Kong Open, winning at the iconic Fanling golf course for the seventh Asian Tour trophy of his career.

The California native carded a sizzling six-under-par 64 in round four to finish 20-under overall, holding off local favourite Matthew Cheung and Finland's Kalle Samooja by five strokes.

Thailand's Jazz Janewattananond and Nick Voke of New Zealand finished tied for fourth at 14-under.

It's Catlin's first triumph on the Asian circuit since the 2024 Saudi Open, and adds to victories in Thailand, Macau, and Malaysia.

Catlin went into the final round locked in a tense four-way tie for the lead at 14-under-par alongside compatriot Caleb Surratt, India's Anirban Lahiri, and Thomas Pieters of Belgium.

But a brilliant performance on the 18th-hole sand solidified his place at the top of the leaderboard.

"There were so many great players, and there was a four-way tie for the lead... anything can happen," Catlin told reporters after the win.

"I just tried to focus on what I can control. I didn't know what anyone else was doing, and I didn't look at the leaderboard until I came down the 18th," he added.

"I just tried to keep focused on the shot at hand, and keep trying to execute good golf shots. History has shown me that it's not over until it's over, and so I just kept pushing forward, giving every shot my full undivided attention. And it paid off... I've got this beautiful trophy here."

Victory in the SAR also came with another milestone for Catlin, who is ranked 447 in the world.

With the Asian Tour tournament a part of The Open Qualifying Series, his strong showing in Fanling earned him a highly coveted qualifying ticket to the 155th edition of the prestigious event, which will be played at the historic Old Course in St Andrews next July.

It also guarantees him his maiden qualification for the Masters Tournament in Augusta, Georgia next year.

"It's kind of a dream come true," Catlin said.

"From the time I can remember, I started playing golf when I was three years old, and my goal was always to play in the Masters. This is my thirteenth year as a professional golfer, and I hadn't had the chance to do so. You just never really know if its going to happen."

articles.title: Families enjoy day out at HK golf open finale
articles.excerpt: Hundreds of fans enjoyed a day out with their families at the Fanling Golf Course on Sunday for the final day of Hong Kong Open action. The four-day event, which is marking its historic 65th edition, teed off on Thursday to much fanfare as the sport's biggest stars descended…
articles.fullText:
Hundreds of fans enjoyed a day out with their families at the Fanling Golf Course on Sunday for the final day of Hong Kong Open action.

The four-day event, which is marking its historic 65th edition, teed off on Thursday to much fanfare as the sport's biggest stars descended upon the SAR.

Hans, a local resident attending the tournament for the second time with his kids, told RTHK that the Hong Kong Open is a great opportunity for families to get up close and personal with some of the world's top athletes.

"It's a great event, walking around with the kids... getting close with the different golf professionals," he said.

"It's an awesome experience, being so close to the professional players and also they do a good job of bringing the fan village together," he added. "It's fun for the kids."

Hans also commended the event's fan-friendly atmosphere, saying the interactive stalls, games, and entertainment made the tournament stand out from other sporting events.

Another local fan, Leon – who is attending the event for the sixth year in a row – echoed the sentiment.

"Personally, I play golf and I'm a member of the club. [This event] has such a nice outdoor area for the kids, every year we take them over and have some fun," he told RTHK.

He also pointed out that there were many elements of Hong Kong culture on display at the fan village.

"[Besides] the golf, we have Hong Kong culture, cultural stuff... which is very fun for the kids. I'd definitely recommend it."

Bryant Lu, captain of the Hong Kong Golf Club, said that the competition is a great opportunity for all sports fans to get a taste of a different side of the bustling city.

"I think what we offer is a very unique experience," he told reporters outside course's clubhouse.

"Being a golfing event we have outdoors... and we can come all the way up to the Northern Metropolis. I think this is the new future for Hong Kong, and hosting an event here not only brings people to play golf but [they can] also experience what changes the Northern Metropolis brings to Hong Kong, I think that's very important."

"I think coming up here you can experience a different side of Hong Kong – beautiful trees, nice grounds, fresh air, and lots of smiling faces."

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Brewers down Rays to take a 2-0 World Series lead
articles.excerpt: The Milwaukee Brewers staged another trademark comeback to defeat the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 and take a commanding 2-0 lead in the best-of-seven World Series on Saturday. The top-seeded Brewers recovered from 4-0 down after an early Tampa Bay onslaught to complete a rally that edges…
articles.fullText:
The Milwaukee Brewers staged another trademark comeback to defeat the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 and take a commanding 2-0 lead in the best-of-seven World Series on Saturday.

The top-seeded Brewers recovered from 4-0 down after an early Tampa Bay onslaught to complete a rally that edges Milwaukee closer to a first Major League Baseball crown.

The win marked the seventh time during this season's playoffs that the Brewers have come from behind to win.

Outfielder Sal Frelick blasted a 408-foot home run in the sixth inning to tie it up for Milwaukee at 4-4 before Cooper Pratt's single in the seventh added what turned out to be the winning run for Brice Turang.

"As long as there's game left we have a chance — and I think we've all bought into that," Pratt said.

"We're never out of it. And when there's still innings on the board we've still got a chance," Pratt added.

Tampa Bay will have the weight of history against them as the series heads back to Florida for game three on Monday.

Only 10 teams have ever recovered from 2-0 down to win the World Series.

Rays manager Kevin Cash believes home-field advantage for the next three games could give Tampa Bay a path back into the series.

"These Milwaukee fans have been really loud. I know our fans are going to be really loud and excited to see us come back and kind of reset ourselves a little bit," Cash said.

"We've got a really good pitcher going, as do they. A lot of confidence in this club to respond. They've done it all season long and they'll continue to do it."

The Rays surged into a commanding 4-0 lead in the top of the first inning with Yandy Diaz scooting to second base after a throwing error by Brewers shortstop Pratt.

Chandler Simpson singled soon afterwards to bring Diaz home and give the Rays a 1-0 lead.

Simpson then used his speed to steal second base and when Junior Caminero drove into the left field, Simpson raced home to score.

The Rays made it 4-0 when catcher Liam Hicks bludgeoned a towering 411-foot two-run homer into the upper deck of right centre-field to further rock the Brewers.

Milwaukee were quick to hit back in the bottom of the inning, with William Contreras singling on a ground ball to score Jackson Chourio.

Garrett Mitchell's single to right field allowed Jake Bauers to score to trim the Rays advantage to two runs.

Milwaukee knocked Tampa Bay starter Drew Rasmussen out of the game in the fourth inning and then pounced with Frelick's home run in the sixth, before Pratt's single in the seventh gave the Brewers the lead.

Brewers reliever Aaron Ashby grabbed the final five outs to secure victory. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Around 1m workers to benefit from MPF Full Portability
articles.excerpt: Around one million workers are set to benefit from an upcoming arrangement that allows employees to transfer not only their own mandatory contributions, but also their employer’s, to an MPF scheme of their choice once every calendar year, the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes…
articles.fullText:
Around one million workers are set to benefit from an upcoming arrangement that allows employees to transfer not only their own mandatory contributions, but also their employer’s, to an MPF scheme of their choice once every calendar year, the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority (MPFA) said on Sunday.

Phase one of the MPF Full Portability scheme is set to begin on December 21.

Employees who joined the workforce or changed jobs on or after May 1 2025 – the day the MPF offsetting arrangement was officially abolished – will be eligible for the first phase.

Writing in a blog post, MPFA chairman Ayesha Lau said the scheme would improve people’s control over their MPF portfolios and encourage employees to manage their retirement reserves more proactively.

She expects the number of beneficiaries to continue to rise as more graduates enter the workforce and employees change jobs.

As for workers who started their current jobs before May 1 2025, Lau noted that because their employer mandatory contributions may continue to be used to offset long service payments or severance payments for employment periods prior to that date, additional legislative amendments would be required to balance operational needs and enhanced employee control.

Transfers for the 2026 calendar year can be made between December 21 and 31, while transfers for 2027 will open on January 1.

Lau pointed out that the new scheme would not change existing arrangements for employers, who would continue to make contributions via the MPF schemes they participate in.

She also reminded workers that the MPF is a long-term investment, advising them to avoid making frequent transfers or switching schemes simply for the sake of it.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: 'Strategic enterprise investments in HK hit HK$28bn'
articles.excerpt: Investments made by the first six batches of firms brought to Hong Kong through the Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises reached HK$28.3 billion as of the end of September, according to Financial Secretary Paul Chan. Writing in his weekly blog, Chan noted that, including…
articles.fullText:
Investments made by the first six batches of firms brought to Hong Kong through the Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises reached HK$28.3 billion as of the end of September, according to Financial Secretary Paul Chan.

Writing in his weekly blog, Chan noted that, including the seventh batch of 18 firms recently welcomed, a total of 142 strategic enterprises have now established or expanded their operations in Hong Kong.

“They are expected to generate around HK$84 billion in investment while creating roughly 27,000 jobs over the coming years,” he said.

“More importantly, these investments are materialising on the ground. As of the end of September this year, actual investments by the first six batches reached HK$28.3 billion while employing over 10,300 people – exceeding the initial phased targets by 30 percent and 34 percent respectively.”

Corporate confidence in Hong Kong is gradually being reflected in real economic outcomes, Chan said.

He added that among the first six batches of enterprises, around 70 percent have established global or regional headquarters in Hong Kong, while nearly 90 percent have set up R&D centres.

Chan said this brings not only capital and jobs, but also research and decision-making functions – both of which are crucial to maintaining Hong Kong’s long-term competitive edge.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Apec meeting showcases HK's role as a bridge: FS
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan on Sunday said hosting the recently concluded Apec Finance Ministers' Meeting carried multi-layered significance for Hong Kong. The two-day event wrapped up in the SAR on Wednesday. Speaking on a Commercial Radio programme, Chan said many…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan on Sunday said hosting the recently concluded Apec Finance Ministers' Meeting carried multi-layered significance for Hong Kong.

The two-day event wrapped up in the SAR on Wednesday.

Speaking on a Commercial Radio programme, Chan said many participants came from the political and business sectors, allowing them to see and understand Hong Kong first-hand and observe how the city serves as a bridge connecting the mainland and the rest of the world.

He pointed out that there are many areas for collaboration and new market opportunities for the SAR’s professional services sector.

“Through communication and exchanges, we understand their needs better. For example, many countries need infrastructure, and infrastructure needs investment, professional services, and even operational management. Some enterprises want to enter the mainland market. We told them that in these areas, they can collaborate with Hong Kong,” he said.

The financial secretary acknowledged that it is sometimes difficult for Apec member economies to reach a consensus on issues, given their differing political stances, development stages, and needs.

But he stressed, Hong Kong would strive to seek common ground while respecting differences, aiming to maximise room for collaboration wherever possible.

Speaking on a TVB programme, Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury Christopher Hui said Hong Kong had demonstrated its soft power in hosting the event.

"The Apec finance ministers issued a joint statement as the meeting concluded. This proves that Hong Kong not only brings people together, but also helps deliver results," he said.

"We can help our country foster regional collaboration across the broader Asian region."

Some delegates also chose to stay behind for a few extra days after the meetings wrapped up to explore more of the city, Hui said.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Obama blasts Trump's 'chaos and cruelty' on campaign
articles.excerpt: Former US president Barack Obama delivered scathing criticisms of his successor, Donald Trump, at rallies Saturday in Ohio and Michigan to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Democrats are attempting to wrest back control of one or both…
articles.fullText:
Former US president Barack Obama delivered scathing criticisms of his successor, Donald Trump, at rallies Saturday in Ohio and Michigan to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

Democrats are attempting to wrest back control of one or both chambers of the US Congress, which are currently controlled by Trump's Republican Party.

The former president retains considerable popularity among the Democratic base, which he is keen to leverage to support his Democratic Party's candidates.

In both states, the 65-year-old former president blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern amid soaring fuel prices.

"The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions," Obama said in Ohio, where he rallied in support of former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown.

"Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for."

"After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, 'Enough is enough,'" Obama declared in Cleveland. "We are voting for change right here in Ohio."

Later, in Michigan, Obama campaigned for Abdul El-Sayed, from the party's left wing, who is in a close race with Republican Mike Rogers for the US Senate.

"Imagine the power duo of Abdul and Elissa," Obama said, referring to the incumbent Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin, who is not up for election this year.

"You got a Muslim man, you got a Jewish woman fighting for you in the United States Senate. That's something, Michigan, you can be proud of."

Obama also urged voters to cast their ballots as soon as possible since early voting is already open in both states.

"Don't procrastinate, don't equivocate," Obama said.

In Ohio, Brown will attempt a comeback against incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while the race for governor will be contested between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate in 2024.

Polls for Ohio give Democrats a slight lead in both those races, but the results are expected to be close.

Obama also took digs at Trump's renovation projects across the US capital, including his botched renovation of the National Mall's Reflecting Pool, his construction of a massive White House Ballroom and the guilded decorations he has adorned the Oval Office with during his second tenure.

"He's got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory," Obama said, referring to popular but indulgent American restaurant chain.

Nationally, polls also suggest that Democrats could regain control of the House of Representatives but face a much more competitive contest for the Senate. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Fresh clashes rock France as protesters march on
articles.excerpt: Clashes erupted across France on Saturday as protesters took to the streets, a week after marches that degenerated into violence and prompted a firm security backlash from President Emmanuel Macron, who is scrambling to restore order. Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as…
articles.fullText:
Clashes erupted across France on Saturday as protesters took to the streets, a week after marches that degenerated into violence and prompted a firm security backlash from President Emmanuel Macron, who is scrambling to restore order.

Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as officers faced "an extremely elevated level of violence" from black-clad "ultra-left" extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.

Riot police squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes.

Two people were "seriously" injured, Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case.

Authorities had deployed 70,000 security personnel across the country for the new marches, called to protest the cost of living.

The violence came a week after rioting that saw public buildings vandalised, hundreds of shops looted and 2,700 people arrested, casting a pall over the country six months before an election to choose Macron's successor.

Nunez said Saturday's outcome was more "positive" than a week ago, with more police on the streets acting more rapidly, conducting more pre-demonstration checks and better protecting businesses.

But there was widespread anger at the government over a protest crackdown viewed as an assault on the right to protest.

Saturday's demonstrations drew between 410,000 and 800,000 people across the country, according to different estimates by authorities and the organising CGT union.

The main Paris march had between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees, according to those sources.

Macron's government has ordered police to prevent protesters reaching city centres, where shops are concentrated, and in Paris and some other cities, partial curfews were imposed in certain urban zones.

The French president had ordered non-union demonstrations be banned as "illegitimate".

In Paris, where many shops had boarded up windows to prevent looting, and the Louvre and the Musee d'Orsay museums shut for the day, the main demonstration passed off largely peacefully.

The march had been pushed to the capital's southeast rim under a last-minute order by authorities.

Afterwards, though, clashes broke out as the crowd was dispersing, with Nunez blaming "500 rioters" at the back of the march.

AFP journalists saw police charge several times, blasting tear gas and using batons against some, mostly young, protesters.

"They were just taking people down, you know, beating protesters," one demonstrator bleeding from a baton blow to his face, who gave his first name as David, told AFP.

Thousands of protesters in the western city of Nantes broke through lines of police firing tear gas and a water cannon to reach the city centre, an AFP journalist witnessed.

Emma, 23, who came out in the northwest city of Rennes, denounced the bans on demonstrations and the "repression" of protests by high school students demanding better learning conditions.

Marching in the rain at the head of the protest in the northern city of Lille, 47-year-old Delphine insisted: "Neither the president, nor the weather will stop me from demonstrating."

In Lyon, police used tear gas to disperse around 1,000 people gathered in the south of the city.

"If they ban protests, that means we're heading more and more towards a regime that is fascist, that is dictatorial," said one 20-year-old protester in Lyon, who gave only his first name, Silem.

In the southern cities of Cannes and Montpellier, far-right activists clashed with "ultra-left militants", in what authorities said was an unprecedented development.

There was looting on the sidelines of the marches in Marseille and Grenoble, police said.

The Yellow Vests, who staged disruptive protests against Macron eight years ago, called for more demonstrations on October 31 for "the freedom to protest".

Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who marched in Paris, said the movement "is going to repeat itself every week".

Tensions were heightened by a rally in the city of Orleans by far-right leader Marine Le Pen's National Rally party to kick off her campaign for the presidential election.

Thousands of counter-protesters chanting anti-fascist slogans marched in the city.

The unrest across France highlighted the febrile political atmosphere ahead of the vote, in which Le Pen leads in surveys.

Inflation in France, particularly affecting the cost of fuel, has surged since the start of the Middle East war in February.

"I'm going to try and instill a bit of optimism," said the four-time presidential hopeful, who has cast herself as the law-and-order candidate, ahead of her first major campaign speech on Sunday.

Protests have also broken out in Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal over different issues, yet with some overlap on inflation and education problems. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Mass rallies for Lula and Bolsonaro on eve of key vote
articles.excerpt: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro wrapped up their campaigns on Saturday ahead of Sunday's presidential runoff vote, mobilising supporters and making a final push for undecided voters. The two candidates have remained neck and neck in…
articles.fullText:
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro wrapped up their campaigns on Saturday ahead of Sunday's presidential runoff vote, mobilising supporters and making a final push for undecided voters.

The two candidates have remained neck and neck in polls following a stronger-than-expected performance by the right-wing senator in the first round.

On Saturday, a CNT/MDA poll showed the senator with a 1.3-point lead.

Lula, who is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, kicked off his last day of campaigning with a march along Rio de Janeiro's iconic Copacabana beach, where thousands of supporters joined the leftist incumbent under a blazing sun.

"We're going to win the election for one simple reason: it's true that the people want change, (but) they want to move forward. They don't want to go backward," Lula told journalists before the rally.

Later, the president led another march in Sao Paulo, passing along Paulista Avenue, a traditional venue for political demonstrations in Brazil's largest city.

"It's so exciting to see everyone here. This is the kind of energy we want for Brazil. Brazil is ours," said Gisele Passos, a 61-year-old businesswoman at the Sao Paulo rally.

For many Lula supporters, the rallies carried a bittersweet undertone.

The 80-year-old president and former union leader is widely expected to be making his final bid for office, lending the campaign's closing events the feel of a farewell tour.

"He's one of a kind. He has had an incredible, remarkable, and hard-fought journey. We're very proud of that," said Olga Leal, a 62-year-old retiree in Sao Paulo.

Bolsonaro, meanwhile, joined a motorcycle caravan in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais, a key battleground state.

No candidate has won the presidency without carrying Minas Gerais since the country's return to democracy in the 1980s.

The senator led Lula by around five percentage points in the state in the first round.

"The time is almost here. There are only a few hours left before we shape the future of our nation for the next 30 or 40 years," said the lawmaker, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, in a social media video.

He later took part in a campaign march in his home state of Rio de Janeiro, which he has represented in the Senate since 2019.

The younger Bolsonaro was first backed by his father to run for the presidency last December.

The former president was sentenced to over 27 years in prison for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 presidential election to Lula.

On Friday, Lula and Bolsonaro met for a final debate on TV Globo, the country's main free-to-air television channel, where they sparred over the cost of living and traded personal attacks. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Houthis claim new strikes on Saudi Arabian targets
articles.excerpt: Yemen's Houthis launched fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia and the seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government on Saturday after blaming the kingdom for strikes that the Iran-backed group said killed 17 people. Saudi Arabia and the government it backs in Yemen have come…
articles.fullText:
Yemen's Houthis launched fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia and the seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government on Saturday after blaming the kingdom for strikes that the Iran-backed group said killed 17 people.

Saudi Arabia and the government it backs in Yemen have come under sustained attack in recent weeks from the Houthis as a years-long truce broke down in the summer, shifting the focus of the wider US-Iran war that erupted in February.

Over the past 24 hours, the Yemeni fighters said they targeted three Saudi airports including the international airport in capital Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an air base.

Military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group launched missiles at "King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the capital of the Saudi enemy, in two phases", the airports in Dammam in the east and Najran in the south.

The group also launched attacks on the southern Khamis Mushait air base as well as "crude oil pumping stations and the crude oil pipeline from east to west".

The Saudi civil defence agency said it had also responded to falling debris in the Mecca and Medina regions on Saturday after intercepting two Houthi missiles.

The Houthis denied targeting the cities, the two holiest in Islam, calling the Saudi claim a "huge lie".

The Houthis also fired at the southern Yemeni city of Aden, the interim seat of the Saudi-backed government, saying they targeted a naval base and military camp overseen by Saudi forces.

Authorities said the coast guards headquarters and a second building of theirs as well as Aden airport had been targeted.

The fresh attack claims came after the Houthis' Al-Masirah TV channel accused the kingdom of separate strikes in Yemen that killed more than a dozen people. Riyadh has not claimed the alleged strikes.

The Houthi broadcaster said a strike on a house in Sanaa killed at least four people, another at a residential building for cement factory workers killed eight and another outside the city of Hodeida killed five from the same family.

Yemen's civil war, pitting the Iran-backed Houthis against the Saudi-supported and internationally recognised government, had been dormant since a ceasefire in 2022, but erupted again in July as the wider Middle East war roiled the region.

Earlier on Saturday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted two missiles targeting Saudi cities Taif and Yanbu in the kingdom's west.

Saudi Arabia's civil defence had broadcast warnings of "potential danger" for four western regions, including Taif and Yanbu as well as Mecca, home to Islam's holiest city.

The warning was lifted minutes later.

The group has also targeted the kingdom's oil infrastructure as well as its airports and tankers.

Yanbu is a major oil export hub on the Red Sea coast that has allowed Riyadh to bypass Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz for much of its crude exports via the east-west pipeline.

An attack on Riyadh airport earlier this month killed 13 people and forced it to shut, while this week the US ordered non-essential embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing the Houthi threat.

Riyadh leads a military coalition that first intervened in 2015 in the conflict, which has devastated Yemen and created one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

The dramatic escalation in Yemen, with the Houthis taking control of the entire Red Sea coast in a lightning offensive last month, has further destabilised the region and disrupted oil markets.

In July, a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen's capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.

The Houthis then declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before launching a major offensive in September in which they seized Yemeni government-held territory along the Red Sea coast.

In response, the Houthis have also reported frequent Saudi strikes targeting areas under their control. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Arsenal level with Man City - thanks to Aston Villa
articles.excerpt: Manchester City's flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton. Tottenham won at Chelsea for just the second time in 42 visits to Stamford…
articles.fullText:
Manchester City's flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton.

Tottenham won at Chelsea for just the second time in 42 visits to Stamford Bridge as Mike Penders's own goal and a Cole Palmer red card cost the Blues in a 2-0 defeat.

Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City's struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons.

Nicolas Jackson struck twice for Unai Emery's men to continue a fine run of form for a new-look Villa side.

Erling Haaland briefly levelled early in the second half, but Maresca was left to rue City not making more of their dominance for large spells of the game.

"We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box," said Maresca.

The Villa side that won the Europa League last season was decimated by high-profile departures during the transfer window.

But Emery has quickly moulded his new squad into shape with Jackson proving his critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea wrong.

The Senegal international pounced on an error by Marc Guehi to fire Villa ahead after just six minutes.

Another of Villa's new signings Zion Suzuki then thwarted City with a string of stunning saves.

Haaland headed in his 13th goal in 10 games this season to equalise.

Villa, though, swiftly responded as Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to keep out Jackson's low shot on the hour mark.

"A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park," said Emery.

"We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic."

Arsenal took advantage to move alongside City on 21 points from eight games with a routine 2-0 win against Everton.

Shorn of the creative inspiration of Bukayo Saka, who is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Arsenal had to rely on their set-piece prowess to get the job done.

Ezri Konsa bundled in his first goal for the club after Everton failed to clear a corner to open the scoring on seven minutes.

Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the lead for Mikel Arteta's men midway through the second period.

"We had some problems to finish the actions but we scored from a set-piece," said Arteta. "That gave us the confidence and composure to go and dominate the game."

Tottenham climbed out of the bottom three as Chelsea self-imploded at the Bridge.

A game hampered by wild weather conditions exploded into action in the final 15 minutes when, on his first Premier League start, Penders, deputising for the injured Emi Martinez, miscued his attempted punch from a Spurs corner over his own line.

Moments later Palmer was dismissed for a second yellow card after catching former team-mate Conor Gallagher.

Spurs took full advantage as Mathys Tel's low strike also deceived Penders to win for only the second time at their London rivals since 1990.

Fulham also moved out of the relegation zone with a 1-0 win at Coventry thanks to Oscar Bobb's individual effort.

On Sunday, the focus turns to Manchester United boss Michael Carrick when his side take on Bournemouth.

A seven-game winless streak has plunged Carrick's future into doubt just months after he was hired on a two-year deal after a successful interim spell in charge at the end of last season. (AFP)

articles.title: Lula and Bolsonaro keep vitriol out of final debate
articles.excerpt: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and senator Flávio Bolsonaro faced off in their second and final debate ahead of Sunday's presidential runoff election, but this time with cooler heads than a few days ago as they tried to reach out to the few undecided voters left…
articles.fullText:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and senator Flávio Bolsonaro faced off in their second and final debate ahead of Sunday's presidential runoff election, but this time with cooler heads than a few days ago as they tried to reach out to the few undecided voters left in the tight race.

Friday's debate on TV Globo lasted two hours and offered candidates a chance to talk about their plans in front of each other.

Five days ago, the two exchanged barbs and accusations in a debate on TV Band.

The latest debate in Rio de Janeiro had three tense moments.

Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, called Lula “nine fingers,” a pejorative nickname used by many of his supporters which references an accident the Brazilian president suffered during his time as a metal worker.

The 80-year-old leader demanded an apology, which Bolsonaro gave him.

“He will have to apologise. Because the working people are watching. Millions of workers suffer accidents due to employer irresponsibility. [They are] being forced to work shifts that we shouldn’t have to work,” said Lula.

“I was underage and I worked at night [when the accident happened].”

The 45-year-old Bolsonaro replied: “Lula, if I offended you by calling you ‘nine-fingers,’ I truly apologise. I didn’t mean to offend you."

The second was when Lula, in response, called Bolsonaro a vigilante, in a reference to groups linked to policemen that are operating in poor communities in Rio de Janeiro.

Bolsonaro said he would rename those groups, called militias, as narcoterrorists.

“I will not allow a vigilante to call me nine fingers,” Lula said.

Bolsonaro was awarded more time by mediators to respond to the insult.

But instead of answering the president's accusation, he chose to talk about a different subject.

The third tense exchange was between Bolsonaro and the mother of a five-year-old girl who was killed in a shootout that involved a policeman who had the presidential candidate as his lawyer.

Bolsonaro said he doesn't believe his client was guilty.

“I am confident that it was not this police officer who fired that shot,” Bolsonaro said.

The child's mother, who was brought by Lula's campaign to the TV Globo studios, yelled from the stands in response: “She is dead.”

On Saturday, both Lula and Bolsonaro are expected to take tens of thousands of supporters to the streets of Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo in their last effort before the runoff.

Bolsonaro won the first round of voting in the presidential election by 47 percent to 45 percent, and recent polls suggest he and Lula, who is seeking his fourth nonconsecutive term, are in a very close race. (AP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Jordan steps up security in wake of church massacre
articles.excerpt: Security was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across Jordan on Saturday, the US embassy in Amman said, a day after a deadly assault on a church that authorities described as a terrorist attack by extremists. Eight people were killed and 40 were injured…
articles.fullText:
Security was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across Jordan on Saturday, the US embassy in Amman said, a day after a deadly assault on a church that authorities described as a terrorist attack by extremists.

Eight people were killed and 40 were injured when gunmen opened fire for several minutes in broad daylight during a funeral at the Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate, the head of Jordan's Public Security Directorate said.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility.

Such attacks are rare in Jordan, although authorities in the US-allied kingdom say they have repeatedly foiled plots by Islamist militants in recent years.

Authorities said they were still searching for the attackers, adding it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan.

"A massacre, a massacre in every sense of the word," said Tarek Ammarin at a hospital where the wounded were being treated.

A relative of Ammarin's was injured in the attack.

Police patrolled on Saturday outside the Hamoud church, about 120 kilometres southwest of the capital Amman.

"This is a result of a terrorist ideology and blind extremism and we will not allow society to go down this path," Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said in a post on X.

Jordan's King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against militant Islamist groups, visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished "with an iron fist".

Christians make up a minority of Jordan's population. The country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Transfusion service brings learning
articles.excerpt: A group of SPHRC Kung Yik She Secondary School students recently received a different kind of biology lesson as they ventured outside of the classroom on a visit to the Yuen Long Blood Donor Centre. The Hong Kong Red Cross Blood Transfusion Service expanded its “A Biology Class…
articles.fullText:
A group of SPHRC Kung Yik She Secondary School students recently received a different kind of biology lesson as they ventured outside of the classroom on a visit to the Yuen Long Blood Donor Centre.

The Hong Kong Red Cross Blood Transfusion Service expanded its “A Biology Class outside of the Classroom” scheme this year. Originally run exclusively at the service’s headquarters, it is now offered at all donor centres, making it much more accessible to school groups.

Real-life settings
Hong Kong Red Cross Blood Transfusion Service Advanced Practice Nurse Lee Wing-sze explained that guided tours, which last an hour, give students the chance to learn in a relaxed and engaging mode.

“As blood-related knowledge is a part of the senior secondary biology curriculum, we integrate these topics into the visit, allowing students to learn within a real-life setting.”

Giving blood
The tour consists of three parts. First, interactive games and information boards are used to introduce basic concepts such as blood types, donor eligibility, and how blood saves lives.

Students then tour the haemoglobin testing area, donation area and blood processing area, learning about overall workflows and the professional equipment involved.

Finally, staff answer questions on the spot to alleviate anxiety and dispel any fears before students make their own decisions on whether to donate blood.

Secondary school student Ryan Yip said that before he experienced the tour, he felt stressed about giving blood.

“I think this whole process is kind of frightening, but after the nurses told me the process is safe and it is all under standard conditions, I think that really comforted me and gave me some confidence to be a voluntary blood donor.”

Another secondary school student, Kelvin To, said he would urge his friends to donate blood after learning about how donations save lives.

Saving lives
The service’s Head of Blood Collection & Donor Recruitment Department Dr Jacky Kong said that establishing a solid foundation of blood-related knowledge is crucial to encouraging teenagers to become blood donors in the long run.

“We believe that interaction with our staff and blood donors is very important for them to be exposed to why blood donation is important for the public.”

The service reaches out to secondary schools across Hong Kong and, to date, has arranged talks or donor centre visits for more than 60 schools in the current academic year.

SPHRC Kung Yik She Secondary School Principal Liu Siu-lin said she fully supports the lessons the service provides as they allow students to witness first-hand how blood is processed and transformed into life-saving products.

“This unique lesson shows that science is not just about cold data, but about saving lives.”

Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki today attended an opening ceremony for two initiatives promoting the Greater Bay Area (GBA) in Dongguan – namely the fourth GBA High-quality Talent Development Conference and the third GBA Doctoral and Postdoctoral Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competition.

Addressing the ceremony, he said Hong Kong will continue to attract the talent required for its own and the country's development, and will work with other GBA cities to advance the alignment of rules and mechanisms that facilitate the flow of talent within the area.

Mr Chan outlined that Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan proactively aligns with the National 15th Five-Year Plan and promotes the integrated development of education, technology and talent. He added that the Northern Metropolis University Town will closely connect Hong Kong's strengths in basic research and internationalised education with both the innovation and technology (I&T) and talent resources of the broader GBA.

After the ceremony, Mr Chan and Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun toured the exhibition hall and visited the Hong Kong Talent Engage booth.

Yesterday, Mr Chan and his delegation visited a key I&T enterprise in Dongguan to better understand the local model of fostering co-operation between the spheres of scientific research, innovation, and talent development. They subsequently toured the City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan) to learn about synergies between Hong Kong and Dongguan in higher education and talent cultivation, and to explore ways of strengthening complementarity between the two places.

Mr Chan and Mr Sun concluded their visit to Dongguan this morning and returned to Hong Kong in the afternoon.

Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) leader Kim Jong-un visited the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday, crossing a newly opened bridge.

Upon his arrival, Kim was met by China's top political advisor Wang Huning, who conveyed greetings from President Xi Jinping, according to Xinhua news agency.

Kim crossed via the New Yalu River Bridge, a major border crossing that officially opened last week, deepening economic ties between China and the DPRK.

The three-kilometre bridge is the most significant land border crossing between both countries.

During a meeting, ​Wang, chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, told Kim that China was ⁠ready to use the bridge's opening to expand personnel exchanges and economic and trade cooperation, Xinhua said.

CCTV reported that Kim took part in a memorial service to pay tribute to martyrs of the Chinese People's Volunteer Army and visited an automobile factory.

His visit came a day before the anniversary of China joining the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, in 1950.

Wang saw Kim off at the bridge at the end of the trip, Xinhua reported. (Agencies)

articles.title: France holds breath as protesters take to streets
articles.excerpt: France was erecting a ring of steel in major cities ahead of new protests on Saturday, with police, helicopters and armoured vehicles seeking to prevent a repeat of the violence and looting which erupted during nationwide demonstrations last weekend. Shops and restaurants in…
articles.fullText:
France was erecting a ring of steel in major cities ahead of new protests on Saturday, with police, helicopters and armoured vehicles seeking to prevent a repeat of the violence and looting which erupted during nationwide demonstrations last weekend.

Shops and restaurants in central Paris were boarded up, the world-famous Louvre and Musee d'Orsay were closed and a curfew was in place for parts of the French capital ahead of hundreds of demonstrations planned across the country.

Weeks of protests by high school students over learning conditions sparked a movement that has since spread nationwide, fuelled by broader anger over the rising cost of living.

But some of the worst urban violence in years exploded on the sidelines of the demonstrations a week ago, which saw more than half a million people turn out.

About 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, while Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu warned late on Friday that "the threat" of violence "remains high".

The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen as the frontrunner and suggesting her position has been strengthened by the latest events.

Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched in the French city of Orleans early on Saturday against a congress by far-right leader Marine Le Pen's National Rally (RN) party there, AFP journalists saw.

"Macron resign. Le Pen in prison," the crowd yelled, while carrying placards that read "The Youth say 'screw you' to the National Rally" and "Hotter than fascists".

Police fired teargas Saturday to disperse some 150 people protesting in the southeastern French city of Lyon, in an area banned to all demonstrations.

Police fired several teargas grenades to clear the group protesting near a university faculty and the city's police station as part of nationwide rallies.

Macron and his government have sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations last Saturday.

Courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, officials said.

Earlier a police helicopter could be seen flying over the city, with security forces patrolling and armoured vehicles and riot police vans parked nearby. Shops were boarded up, with private security guards in front of some. Calls to defy the bans on protests in the city centre had circulated on social media. (AFP)

articles.excerpt: The Department of Health (DH) said on Saturday that the email account for its HIV testing service website was suspected of being misused. Emails and text messages had been sent to the public under the guise of the department, claiming the recipients were exposed to Human…
articles.fullText:
The Department of Health (DH) said on Saturday that the email account for its HIV testing service website was suspected of being misused.

Emails and text messages had been sent to the public under the guise of the department, claiming the recipients were exposed to Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) and should seek medical advice and get tested as soon as possible, according to the DH.

The department said it is conducting a thorough investigation of the incident, stressing that it would not notify individuals in this manner.

“Upon discovering the incident last night, DH staff immediately conducted a comprehensive inspection of the network system with the outsourced service provider and investigated the incident overnight,” it said.

“So far, no data loss or leakage has been detected. The DH reported the incident to the police and notified the Digital Policy Office.”

The DH added that its HIV testing service website had been suspended from Saturday for the investigation, but members of the public could still book for HIV tests via phone calls.

articles.excerpt: Thirty-three people have been arrested after Hong Kong and Shenzhen officers busted a cross-boundary credit card fraud syndicate that allegedly targeted SAR residents travelling to Shenzhen. The gang is believed to be linked to at least 60 fraud cases involving amount of more…
articles.fullText:
Thirty-three people have been arrested after Hong Kong and Shenzhen officers busted a cross-boundary credit card fraud syndicate that allegedly targeted SAR residents travelling to Shenzhen.

The gang is believed to be linked to at least 60 fraud cases involving amount of more than HK$1.8 million, according to the police.

Chief inspector Fung Chi-tat said police had received multiple complaints from residents whose credit cards were stolen and used to buy mobile phones.

“Investigations showed that these people had been to popular tourist spots or entertainment venues in Shenzhen but had not checked up on their belongings at those places,” he said.

“It was only after they were informed by their banks of unusual, large-value credit card transactions that they realised their cards had been stolen and used.”

Superintendent Tsang Chun-kit said the gang stole credit cards from Hong Kong residents in Shenzhen and brought the cards back to the SAR immediately to shop at different stores.

The suspects would then resell the items the same day before fleeing Hong Kong.

Tsang added that the syndicate had mistakenly believed they could evade arrest by fleeing the SAR.

However, he said, the Hong Kong police force has been in close communication with mainland law enforcement authorities.

Sixteen of the arrests – 11 men and five women aged between 17 and 45 – were made in Hong Kong while Public Security Bureau officers in Shenzhen picked up 11 men and six women aged 36 to 56.

articles.title: Moonshot tweaks the hack out of latest AI model
articles.excerpt: Moonshot AI has reduced the cyber-offensive capabilities of its newest model, the Chinese startup said on Saturday, as fears grow that increasingly autonomous artificial intelligence could turbocharge hacking. Beijing-based Moonshot announced the curbs while introducing Kimi…
articles.fullText:
Moonshot AI has reduced the cyber-offensive capabilities of its newest model, the Chinese startup said on Saturday, as fears grow that increasingly autonomous artificial intelligence could turbocharge hacking.

Beijing-based Moonshot announced the curbs while introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, which it describes as its most capable three-trillion-parameter-class open-weight model. The company plans to publish the model's weights – files allowing outside developers to run and modify it on their own systems – by November 4.

Moonshot said it removed cyber-related data from the training corpus and reinforcement-learning environments used to develop the model while retaining general coding skills.

"We aim not to release open weights that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability," the company said.

Governments, technology companies and security researchers are growing increasingly concerned that AI could make sophisticated hacking easier and cheaper. Models that can write code, operate software tools and complete long, multi-step tasks may help users identify weaknesses in programs and automate parts of cyberattacks.

China proposed export controls last week that would ban exports of AI-driven malware-generation and mutation technology and restrict AI-assisted vulnerability-discovery tools.

The draft measures, which remain open for public comment, cite the risk that such capabilities could be used against critical infrastructure, defence-industrial and core government systems, or to bypass security protections.

Moonshot said open-weight models can improve security by helping more organisations inspect and secure their own software, including older systems that receive little attention.

Unlike proprietary, closed-weight AI systems, however, open-weight releases make central oversight more difficult. Once the files are widely distributed, the original developer has less ability to restrict access, monitor use or update safeguards than with a hosted service.

K3.1 Pro scored 81 percent on its internal cyber benchmark, compared with 90.5 percent for a similar version without the risk-reduction measures, the company said. The test involved finding and exploiting software vulnerabilities in a controlled environment.

Moonshot said the comparison showed that filtering cyber-related data reduced the model's offensive cyber performance, although it still outperformed its predecessor. The results have not been independently verified.

K3.1 Pro has a one-million-token context window, allowing it to process very large amounts of text at once. Moonshot also released a faster version, K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which it said runs at two to three times the speed of the standard model. (Reuters)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Brewers win World Series opener in nail-biting finish
articles.excerpt: Trevor Megill struck out Jonny DeLuca with runners on second and third to wriggle out of a ninth-inning jam as the Milwaukee Brewers escaped with a 3-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays in game one of the World Series. DeLuca's strikeout on Friday night came after Tampa Bay's Liam…
articles.fullText:
Trevor Megill struck out Jonny DeLuca with runners on second and third to wriggle out of a ninth-inning jam as the Milwaukee Brewers escaped with a 3-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays in game one of the World Series.

DeLuca's strikeout on Friday night came after Tampa Bay's Liam Hicks had grounded into an apparent game-ending double play that was overturned after a video review.

Replays determined that Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt's right foot was slightly off the bag when he reached to catch a high throw from second baseman Brice Turang.

Jacob Misiorowski allowed one run over five innings to earn the win.

Christian Yelich hit an RBI triple to spark a two-run rally in the first inning that put the Brewers ahead for good and delighted a sellout crowd revelling in Milwaukee’s first World Series game since 1982.

Jackson Chourio and William Contreras provided two hits each, and Contreras also threw out two potential base stealers.

This marks the first World Series featuring two potential first-time champions since 1980, when the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Kansas City Royals in six games.

The only other major league teams without a World Series title are the Colorado Rockies, San Diego Padres and Seattle Mariners.

The game one winner has gone on to win the World Series 62.8 percent of the time.

Tampa Bay trailed 3-1 and hadn't put a runner on since the sixth inning until it mounted its comeback try in the ninth.

Jonathan Aranda and Chandler Simpson hit consecutive one-out singles off Megill.

A double steal involving pinch-runner Jorge Mateo and Simpson put the potential tying run in scoring position with Rays slugger Junior Caminero at the plate.

Caminero walked on a 3-2 pitch in the dirt to load the bases.

Hicks hit a grounder to the right side, and Turang ranged well to his left to field the ball before throwing to Pratt to start what initially was ruled a game-ending double play.

But a replay review determined Pratt’s right foot came off the bag as he caught Turang’s throw.

Hicks was still out at first, but the Rays now had runners at second and third with the score 3-2.

Megill finally closed the deal as DeLuca struck out swinging.

By sweeping the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, the Brewers had time to set up their rotation the way they wanted by handing the Game 1 start to Misiorowski, the hard-throwing NL Cy Young Award favourite.

Misiorowski opened the game by throwing the fastest pitch ever delivered in a World Series game, a 103.5 mph ball to Yandy Díaz.

The right-hander ended up allowing only one run over five innings with a season-low three strikeouts. (AP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

The pair also said they hope to qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics and win gold at the Games.

In the mixed BC1/BC2 team event, the SAR trio of John Loung, Yeung Hiu-lam and Chan Pak-lun defeated South Korea 7-5 to take home the bronze medal.

articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump on Friday said another military operation could be carried out against Iran just as the war nears its eight-month mark and rising fuel prices weigh on the US midterm elections.

"We may do another little Epic Fury," Trump told a rally in Florida, using the US military's term for its war on Iran. He did not elaborate.

Trump said earlier in the day the United States could end the war quickly, but questioned whether Washington should seek a swift conclusion or allow the conflict to gradually wind down.

Trump, who has offered shifting goals and timelines for the war, has said in recent campaign remarks that the war will end soon, "one way or the other".

He said earlier this month the US would not launch an attack on Iran before the November 3 elections that would determine control of Congress, where Trump's Republican Party holds a narrow majority in both chambers.

The United States and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, and Tehran responded with its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases.

US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon have killed thousands and displaced millions.

The war has raised oil and gas prices around the world.

Tehran plans a wider retaliation if the war resumes, Iranian officials said.

Iran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the United States and Israel attack again, according to two senior security officials in Tehran. (Reuters)

articles.excerpt: Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan on Saturday said a newly launched scheme that eases cross-border yacht visits would usher in a new wave of tourist consumption. Speaking on an RTHK radio programme, she said the first batch of five mainland vessels that entered…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan on Saturday said a newly launched scheme that eases cross-border yacht visits would usher in a new wave of tourist consumption.

Speaking on an RTHK radio programme, she said the first batch of five mainland vessels that entered the city last Friday through the southbound yacht scheme stayed for three to four days.

Some of them reserved hotels in advance of their overnight stays.

Those who docked at Lantau Yacht Club could use their craft as accommodation, Chan said, but they would still go on shore to spend.

“Some of them visited Stanley, some even headed to Central,” she said.

“Apart from sightseeing at sea, they would also go on shore to shop and head to theme parks.”

Yacht owners and masters have to register an account with the SAR’s Marine Department as part of the procedure for them to travel here, with Chan saying 32 accounts have already been set up so far.

She also said that, ahead of the end of the application period for platform companies to apply for ride-hailing service licences on October 30, the government is considering allowing applicants who are, for instance, particularly able to meet Hong Kong's needs, to have a higher chance of securing a permit.

A lottery will be carried out if the number of applications exceeds the 10,000-permit cap.

“I think that some of the main considerations include whether they are able to provide transport capacity or if they are really committed – this is very important," Chan said.

"We will also take into consideration how long they have owned the vehicles.”

Since a new combined written test for taxis and ride-hailing vehicles was launched in early August as part of the new regulatory framework for ride-hailing services, Chan said around 16,000 people have registered for the exam so far.

The government was, she stressed, pleased to see the enthusiastic response to the test, which has seen a passing rate of more than 60 percent.

Advanced technologies and additional manpower have been deployed at Huanggang Port to ensure smooth border crossings, Commissioner of Customs and Excise Chan Tsz-tat said on Saturday.

Speaking after a Commercial Radio programme, he said customs clearances at the redeveloped port had been smooth.

“We have deployed some staff from other control points," Chan said.

"We have also employed some temp staff and retired officers to be deployed at the Huanggang Port to support the new operation.

“We also employed some new technologies at our new control point.

“We are seeing quite good effectiveness in deterrence of smuggling at the new Huanggang Port.

"If these new equipment are effective, we intend to extend the application of these new detection devices to other control points.”

Chan also said more than 600 million illicit cigarettes were seized in the first three quarters of the year – about the same as the full-year figure recorded in 2025.

However, he pointed out that more than 200 million of them were not destined for Hong Kong, but were in the process of being transhipped to other places.

Chan said the department had seen “very good enforcement results” so far this year and that he believed they would deter smugglers.
