In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index rebounded back above 23,000 to open up 93 points, or 0.41 percent, at 23,027.

The China Enterprises Index was 55 points, or 0.72 percent, higher at 7,744 while the tech index moved 19 points, or 0.51 percent, up to 3,813.

Further north, the Shanghai Composite Index opened down 34 points, or 0.94 percent, at 3,623 while the blue-chip CSI300 index lost 1.1 percent.

Both key mainland indices added to losses from the previous session, when the CSI300 posted its lowest close since July 2025 and the Shanghai benchmark ended at its weakest level in more than a year.

The CSI300 index is now down more than 20 percent from its most recent closing peak on June 22, meeting some definitions for confirmation of a "bear market". By the most widely accepted definition of the term, it has been in one ever since a 2007 closing-level high.

"Three converging forces: a deepening selloff in AI-related technology stocks, escalating Middle East tensions following deadly attacks on Saudi Aramco infrastructure, and intensifying stress in French sovereign debt markets, triggered a sharp risk-off rotation across global markets overnight," analysts at UOB said in a note.

The Shenzhen Component Index opened down 169 points, or 1.49 percent, at 11,187 while the ChiNext Index opened down 42 points, or 1.66 percent, at 2,534.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 240 points, or 0.38 percent, lower at 62,667, plunged straight down after that to 61,528 and was 1,239 points in the red at one stage before noon.

articles.title: 76ers storm back to stun Cavs in home opener
articles.excerpt: The Philadelphia 76ers erased a 29-point deficit to stun the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106 on Thursday in NBA superstar LeBron James' first home game since landing in Philly as a free agent. Tyrese Maxey scored 32 points and Joel Embiid added 24, including a jump shot with 6:54…
articles.fullText:
The Philadelphia 76ers erased a 29-point deficit to stun the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106 on Thursday in NBA superstar LeBron James' first home game since landing in Philly as a free agent.

Tyrese Maxey scored 32 points and Joel Embiid added 24, including a jump shot with 6:54 left to play that gave the Sixers their first lead of the night, one they wouldn't relinquish.

Former Celtics star Jaylen Brown, the Sixers' other big off-season acquisition, scored 21 points and pulled down eight rebounds and four-time NBA champion James added 17 points, 10 rebounds and five assists to help the 76ers author their biggest comeback of the play-by-play era that started in 1996.

Cleveland, disappointed not to land hometown hero James after he announced he was leaving the Los Angeles Lakers after eight seasons, appeared to be on a mission to show him what he missed.

James won one of his four championships with Cleveland, and Cavs coach Kenny Atkinson admitted before the game that James's decision to pursue a fifth crown with the 76ers left him "just depressed, honestly" for the first couple of days after the move was announced.

But he had reason to be pleased with the Cavaliers' start to their first game of the new season.

Donovan Mitchell scored 22 of his 32 points in the first half as the Cavs seized control against a 76ers team struggling to find a rhythm and protect the ball.

Philadelphia's Joel Embiid looked creaky, and James had five of the Sixers' 15 first-half turnovers, which led to 22 Cavs points and provoked boos from Philly fans whose hopes of a title run have been raised by the arrivals of James and Brown.

The boos turned to raucous cheers as the re-energised 76ers opened the third quarter on an 11-0 run. They cut the lead to single digits on back-to-back baskets from Maxey that pulled them within 80-73.

The Cavs were struggling to regroup. Maxey reduced the deficit to two points with a running finger roll layup with 2:33 left in the third before Cleveland reeled off six straight points to take a 90-82 lead into the fourth quarter.

But the 76ers kept coming. They out-scored the Cavaliers 60-37 in the second half, clamping down defensively and giving up just two turnovers.

Evan Mobley scored 18 points for Cleveland but had just three in the second half. Jarrett Allen scored 14 but was held scoreless after the break. (AFP)

articles.title: 'Daily Huanggang traffic hit 130k at long weekend'
articles.excerpt: The new Huanggang border crossing facility is operating smoothly but still has room for improvement, Secretary for Security Chris Tang said on Friday, as he revealed that daily passenger traffic hit 130,000 during the three-day Chung Yeung festival holiday. Speaking on a radio…
articles.fullText:
The new Huanggang border crossing facility is operating smoothly but still has room for improvement, Secretary for Security Chris Tang said on Friday, as he revealed that daily passenger traffic hit 130,000 during the three-day Chung Yeung festival holiday.

Speaking on a radio programme, Tang said the new port is handling about 83,000 passengers on ordinary days – more than double the volume of the old crossing.

During the long weekend holiday period, the average daily figure reached 130,000, with the busiest period around midday on Saturday, seeing waits of up to one hour from alighting to completing clearance, the security minister said.

"On the 17th, the number of people exiting was nine times higher than normal. Usually, during peak hours, the wait is 15 minutes; now, it’s nine times longer than peak hours – if you calculate it that way, you might have to wait two hours. Also, don’t forget that this time, our border crossing allows direct entry into the mainland. Previously, after exiting Hong Kong, you still had to queue again on the mainland," he said.

Tang stressed that the "one-stop" inspection system still makes the process faster than before, as travellers only need to go through a single check.

The minister identified several areas for improvement, saying some travellers have not pre-registered for e-channel services, and children under seven must use manual counters. He said the authorities would learn from the experience and step up crowd management.

On arrangements for non-Chinese passport holders, Tang said the mainland side requires them to fill in forms, and Hong Kong authorities have been assisting travellers in completing the paperwork while they wait.

Tang noted that the new crossing can open up to 90 departure counters – 60 e-channels and 30 manual counters. However, the manual counters require staff on both the SAR and the mainland sides to operate simultaneously.

The security chief thanked frontline staff for their hard work, acknowledging they are under immense pressure and have had to cancel leave. He said the authorities have deployed additional manpower and extended working hours where necessary.

On next month's Apec summit in Shenzhen, Tang said if any Very Important Persons travel via Hong Kong, security preparations must be thorough, though the impact on ordinary citizens is expected to be minimal.

He said the authorities will guard against anyone using Hong Kong as a gateway to enter the mainland for illegal activities, and will also watch for drone activity aimed at disrupting the summit.

articles.title: Japan braces for rate hike as inflation accelerates
articles.excerpt: Inflation in Japan accelerated sharply in September, official data showed on Friday, rising above the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) target level and paving the way for a further interest rate hike. The acceleration was driven in particular by rising prices for processed foods against a…
articles.fullText:
Inflation in Japan accelerated sharply in September, official data showed on Friday, rising above the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) target level and paving the way for a further interest rate hike.

The acceleration was driven in particular by rising prices for processed foods against a backdrop of soaring energy costs owing to the conflict in the Middle East.

Excluding volatile fresh produce, inflation was 2.1 percent, up from 1.7 percent in August, according to the internal affairs ministry reading.

The figure was in line with market expectations and above the 2.0 percent target set by the central bank, further raising chances of an interest rate hike.

"With underlying inflation back above the Bank of Japan's 2 percent target, the case for further tightening remains on solid ground," said Abhijit Surya of Capital Economics.

"News reports suggest that the Bank may revise up its inflation forecasts at its October meeting. That should set the stage for another hike in December."

The BoJ already raised interest rates in mid-September, in line with other major central banks around the world, in an effort to counter strong inflationary pressures driven by soaring energy prices triggered by the Iran war.

A weak yen is also driving up the price of imported goods.

Rents and automobile-related costs also contributed to inflation, the data showed.

Surya, of Capital Economics, said rent inflation matched "its highest rate in nearly 25 years".

But government support for petrol and electricity fees mitigated the impact on energy prices, according to the internal affairs ministry.

Excluding both food and energy, inflation stood at 2.4 percent, above market expectations, following a figure of 1.9 percent in August.

The government is trying to mitigate the impact of inflation on household purchasing power, notably with a massive stimulus package adopted at the end of 2025 and extensive tax breaks on energy.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's two predecessors were undone by anger over inflation.

The government said it would slash consumption tax on food products from eight percent to one percent for two years, starting in April.

However media reports said this will cost the government 10 trillion yen, or about US$63 billion, in lost tax revenues.

articles.title: France's Macron tightens curbs on protests
articles.excerpt: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that "illegitimate" protests would be banned in the coming days and blamed "seditious" ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend's riots and looting. Speaking after a meeting with intelligence chiefs and senior ministers…
articles.fullText:
French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that "illegitimate" protests would be banned in the coming days and blamed "seditious" ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend's riots and looting.

Speaking after a meeting with intelligence chiefs and senior ministers, Macron said demonstrations organised by groups such as trade unions would be allowed to go ahead but could be diverted along alternative routes to protect businesses.

"Last Saturday we had political and seditious acts by ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic," he said.

His comments came as authorities across France prepared for fresh protests following some of the country's worst urban unrest in years.

Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said he wanted voting rights suspended for people who defy bans on taking part in demonstrations, and restrictions on social media access for people involved in violence, looting or attacks on police.

All protests planned for Saturday in Marseille and Lyon, France's second- and third-largest cities, have been banned, local authorities said. Yet fresh demonstrations are already taking shape before what officials fear could be another volatile weekend.

France's main student union, UNEF, has called for rallies on Saturday, while the Yellow Vest movement, the anti-establishment force that emerged in 2018, has filed plans for a march through central Paris.

Businesses in central Paris have begun boarding up their shop windows in case of violence. Luxury goods group Hermes said it had stepped up security measures at its French stores.

Organisers of the Art Basel Paris international art collectors fair being held in a central Paris exhibition hall said it would be closed all weekend.

Elsewhere, authorities in the northern city of Orleans were bracing for potential unrest as the far-right National Rally was due to hold an annual meeting and unions and left-wing groups planned demonstrations.

A student protest called for Thursday in Paris was initially banned but eventually allowed to go ahead, though metro stations in central Paris were nonetheless shuttered by transit authorities in anticipation of unauthorised gatherings.

France was rocked on October 17 by violence on the fringes of nationwide protests, exposing the depth of public anger and raising questions about the security services' ability to keep order.

Two people have been arrested over an arson attack on Limoges city hall, French officials and media said.

A third consecutive night of local curfews passed without major incidents in areas affected by the violence, offering the government some respite ahead of the weekend. (Reuters)

articles.title: Sri Lanka beat England with second-highest ODI chase
articles.excerpt: Janith Liyanage smashed a six off the penultimate ball as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, scoring 430-8 to beat England in Rawalpindi on Thursday. Needing eight to win off the last over, Sri Lanka lost two wickets to paceman Josh…
articles.fullText:
Janith Liyanage smashed a six off the penultimate ball as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, scoring 430-8 to beat England in Rawalpindi on Thursday.

Needing eight to win off the last over, Sri Lanka lost two wickets to paceman Josh Tongue, but Liyanage kept his cool to achieve an astonishing victory and overshadow Harry Brook's record-setting knock.

The England captain hit the fastest-ever ODI double hundred, making 202 off 116 balls to propel his team to a mammoth 429-4 after they were put in to bat.

South Africa hold the record for the highest ODI chase, knocking off a target of 435 against Australia at Johannesburg in 2006.

Batters thoroughly dominated in Rawalpindi as Brook also hit the first ODI double century by an England player. However, Sri Lanka proved up to the challenge as Pavan Rathnayake scored 130, with Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both making 97.

Liyanage then led them over the line with a blistering 61 not out off 27 balls.

Sri Lanka slid to 24-2 before Rathnayake and Avishka set about transforming the innings, putting on 166 for the third wicket.

Rathnayake then combined with Shanaka to lift the tempo with a rapid 133-run stand off just 79 balls, to give Sri Lanka genuine hope.

Rathnayake hit 15 fours and three sixes while Shanaka's blazing knock featured eight sixes and six fours, as Sri Lanka delivered a powerful response to Brook's earlier masterclass.

Sri Lankan skipper Kusal Mendis was delighted at the victory.

"I'm very happy as a captain," said Mendis. "Everyone believed we can do it. Every day we talk about showing the character in team meetings, and it's about showing we can get any score."

Brook was full of praise for Sri Lanka.

"Incredible game of cricket, both teams were exceptional. They played exceptional cricket to knock off 400," said Brook, downplaying his double hundred.

"It was a nice innings but being on the losing side it has no value whatsoever in my eyes."

Brook clobbered 10 sixes and 21 fours as England posted a first 400-plus ODI total in Pakistan.

He reached 200 in 114 balls, beating the previous fastest double century in ODIs, by Shubman Gill (117 balls) for India against West Indies last month.

Brook was joined in the fireworks by Joe Root, who scored a 66-ball 69 and became the first England batter to complete 8,000 runs, in his 197th one-day international.

Brook was dismissed off the final delivery, caught off paceman Liyanage, but not before helping England add 156 runs in the last 10 overs.

Opener Tom Banton set the tone with a 51-ball 50 and Will Jacks was 66 not out with three sixes and eight fours.

The day looked as if it would surely belong to history-maker Brook, but Sri Lanka had other ideas as the previous highest ODI total at a Pakistan venue of 375-3 was easily surpassed.

Pakistan, who beat Sri Lanka and England in their two games, will face England in Lahore on Sunday in the next match in the tri-series. (AFP)

articles.title: Bournemouth stun 10-man AC Milan in Europa League
articles.excerpt: Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan on Thursday to make it three wins from their opening three games in the Europa League. Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier converted first-half penalties to put Bournemouth firmly in control against AC…
articles.fullText:
Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan on Thursday to make it three wins from their opening three games in the Europa League.

Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier converted first-half penalties to put Bournemouth firmly in control against AC Milan, one of Europe's leading clubs.

Milan goalkeeper and skipper Mike Maignan was red carded early on for a foul on Tyler Adams and his side never fully recovered.

Amine Adli scored a sublime 84th free-kick to make it 3-0, the Premier League side having opened their inaugural Europa League campaign with victory at Real Sociedad followed by a 3-0 home win over Sturm Graz last week.

Bournemouth, who became the first English club since Sunderland in 1973/74 to win the first three European fixtures in their history, will now face Sparta Prague and Celta Vigo in November.

"It means a lot. We came off two victories, so that gave us a good feeling for this game," Kluivert told TNT Sports.

"We trust ourselves. It doesn't matter who we play against. We know what we're capable of, and I think we showed that today."

Bournemouth's Premier League rivals Crystal Palace rebounded from a 5-0 weekend thrashing by Brighton to claim a 2-2 draw with Beskitas in Istanbul, while Scottish giants Celtic suffered a third successive defeat, going down 2-1 to Celta Vigo.

Bayer Leverkusen, however, also made it three straight wins with a Jonas Hofmann double earning a 2-0 away win at OFI Crete as both Juventus and Sunderland lost ground in Thursday's third matchday.

The once mighty Hungarian side Ferencvaros kept pace with Leverkusen on nine points thumping Portuguese outfit Torreense 4-1, while Belgium's Union Saint-Gilloise won 4-0 against Israeli outfit Hapoel Be'er Sheva.

Saint-Gilloise, Sunderland and Juve all have seven points from three games.

Juventus thought they had come from behind to beat French side Rennes but had their late 'winner' ruled out for a marginal offside.

Zeki Celik put Juve ahead after five minutes only for a poor clearance 10 minutes later allowing Musa Al-Taamari to poke home an equaliser. Jut before the break Boulaye Dia put the visitors ahead.

Juventus made it 2-2 thanks to a handball and a spot-kick transformed by Nick Woltemade before VAR provided the biggest talking point, disallowing Jhon Lucumi's 88th minute strike.

Clad in a new all-pink kit, Sunderland were left kicking themselves after a 1-1 draw in Poland.

The Blacks Cats took a second minute lead in Poznan thanks to Timur Tutierov and dominated the game without being able to close out the win.

With two home games remaining, however, the second round still beckons for Regis Le Bris' side.

Marseille went down 1-0 to Sturn Graz while Lyon suffered a 3-0 thrashing at the hands of Hoffenheim.

In the Conference League, former Liverpool striker Mohamed Salah opened the scoring from the penalty spot in Trabzonspor's 2-0 win over Scottish side Hearts.

Brighton were held to a 0-0 draw at Czech side Jablonec, as Monaco thumped Freiburg 3-0 and Ajax snuck a 2-0 win over Atalanta. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: US stocks fall as AI doubts ignite tech selloff
articles.excerpt: US stocks tumbled on Thursday and the Nasdaq posted its steepest daily drop since early June as a batch of high-profile earnings reports ignited fresh fears about the AI spending race. The S&P 500 ended deep in negative territory. But the tech-laden Nasdaq, dragged down by…
articles.fullText:
US stocks tumbled on Thursday and the Nasdaq posted its steepest daily drop since early June as a batch of high-profile earnings reports ignited fresh fears about the AI spending race.

The S&P 500 ended deep in negative territory. But the tech-laden Nasdaq, dragged down by microchips, suffered a steeper loss, falling 2.6 percent in the wake of a spate of high-profile AI-related earnings results.

The blue-chip Dow eked out a nominal gain minutes before the closing bell.

Meta Platforms' results beat analyst expectations, but its stock slid 7 percent as the Facebook parent posted its first cash outflow in more than a decade due to its AI-related expenditures and announced plans to issue non-voting shares in a two-for-one split to raise capital to spend on the nascent technology.

Tesla shares fell 3.1 percent even though the electric car maker unexpectedly posted positive free cash flow in the quarter and cut its 2026 capital spending plans.

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index, which has driven much of the current bull market's gains, plunged 6.7 percent, its biggest daily percentage drop since June 23.

"It's a wonderful day on Wall Street," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser & market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois. "The only part of the market that is really suffering here is technology, which has been the golden child of the markets up until about June."

"Investors are starting to realise that there are some holes in the AI story," Nolte added. "And that's having an impact on the indices because they're so heavily weighted toward technology."

On the geopolitical stage, Iran-backed Houthis launched new strikes against Saudi targets, sending crude prices to a five-month high. Investors worried that ongoing Middle East strife could keep inflation hot and force the US Federal Reserve to keep raising interest rates.

Data from the US Labour Department showed initial claims for unemployment benefits kept drifting along near multi-decade lows. Signs of labour market stability will allow the Fed to focus on fighting inflation. Financial markets are currently pricing in the probability that the central bank will raise its policy rate by another 25 basis points before year-end.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 11 points, or 0.02 percent, to 52,867, the S&P 500 lost 93 points, or 1.2 percent, to 7,663 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 694 points, or 2.6 percent, to 26,008.

Third-quarter earnings season is well underway, with 111 of the companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 83 percent have beaten analyst expectations, according to the most recent LSEG data.

Procter & Gamble warned that rising cost pressures would take an increasing bite out of profit, but beat analyst estimates, sending the stock 5.6 percent higher and supporting consumer staples.

Blackstone advanced 8.4 percent, after the company said widening credit spreads on AI-related debt could present an opportunity to lock in higher returns.

Lockheed Martin climbed 7 percent after the aerospace/defence firm raised its annual sales and profit forecast.

Spotify rose 11.1 percent after the Swedish music streaming firm forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates, betting on its AI-powered features to drive user growth.

Chipmakers Intel, AMD, Sandisk and Marvell all tumbled more than 8 percent amid the broader semiconductor selloff. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Magnitude-7 quake kills at least 16 in Xizang
articles.excerpt: At least 16 people have been killed and 32 others injured after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Baqen County in the northeastern part of the Xizang Autonomous Region on Thursday evening. Xinhua news agency reported that more than 300 houses have collapsed. Power was cut off…
articles.fullText:
At least 16 people have been killed and 32 others injured after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Baqen County in the northeastern part of the Xizang Autonomous Region on Thursday evening.

Xinhua news agency reported that more than 300 houses have collapsed. Power was cut off and telecommunications services were disrupted in the county seat of Baqen, some 70 kilometres away from the township of Maru where the quake was centred.

Tremors were also felt in other parts of Xizang, including Qamdo and Nyingchi.

The report said as of 2.25am on Friday, 11 of the injured were in serious condition while 21 sustained minor injuries.

The office of the State Council earthquake relief headquarters and the Ministry of Emergency Management activated a Level-IV emergency response after the tremor, while Xizang has activated a Level-II earthquake disaster emergency response, according to the regional emergency command centre.

More than 300 police officers have been dispatched to the epicentre for relief work while the regional fire and rescue corps has mobilised 347 personnel to the affected areas.

The China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC) said the quake struck at 10.33pm on Thursday at a depth of 10 kilometres. A separate, 4.3-magnitude quake struck Zadoi County in neighbouring Qinghai province some 40 minutes after the initial tremor.

Strong quakes were felt in townships along the border between the two counties, Xinhua reported, with cracks appearing in some houses. However, no building collapses or casualties were immediately reported. (Reporting by Xinhua)

articles.title: ‘I hope that she will be free before long’ Aung San Suu Kyi’s son Kim Aris says
articles.excerpt: Kim Aris talks to RFA after his first direct contact in 5 years with his mother, under house arrest in Myanmar.
articles.fullText:
Myanmar’s military-backed government announced on Thursday that former leader Aung San Suu Kyi – currently under house arrest – was allowed to talk for 20 minutes to her son Kim Aris at 2:30 p.m. via a call placed to the Myanmar embassy in London, where Aris resides.
He speaks in an exclusive interview with Radio Free Asia.
Radio Free Asia: After more than five years without direct contact, how did you get the opportunity to speak with your mother and how did the Myanmar Embassy in London reach out to you? How was the call arranged?
Kim Aris: I was informed through the British Foreign Office here that the call may take place. This was last week. And then earlier this week, they confirmed that it would take place, and they accompanied me to the Burmese Embassy this morning.
RFA: During your conversation, did Daw Aung San Suu Kyi mention anything about her health or her daily life?
Kim Aris: Well, she was more concerned about my health and the rest of the family than anything else. But obviously, I asked after her health and how things were, where she is. She wasn’t able to reveal too much, but I know that she’s been held in some residence, I believe in Naypyidaw, and she sounds healthy. But at the same time, I know that she is in some pain because her hand is not very well; she has tendonitis. So at times, the pain is quite extreme, and I think she is even unable to use that hand at times. Nothing too clear. I know that she’s getting a regular six-monthly checkup, but I know that will be a military doctor, so it’s not like having her own personal doctor.
RFA: Do you know whether she has any access to news from the outside world?
Kim Aris: I don’t think she does. As far as I’m aware, she has no radio or television and doesn’t get any newspapers or anything like that. We know that the conversation will have been monitored and recorded, so we can’t talk about anything sensitive. Besides which, there was a lot to talk about just talking about what’s happened in the family over the last five years. So that’s what we talked about.
RFA: During these recent developments , do you believe there could be a political breakthrough on the horizon?
Kim Aris: I sincerely hope so. I think everybody is tired of the fighting now, and people are starting to think that they need to start talking to each other. But I think the first thing that needs to happen before anybody will start talking is the political prisoners, including may may (Burmese expression for “mom”), need to be freed.
RFA: Some observers believe the Myanmar authorities may be looking for a way out of Myanmar’s ongoing political crisis. What is your take on this?
Kim Aris: Well, it’s very clear the military have been trying to be more appealing to the international community, especially following their elections at the end of last year and the beginning of this year. So they are doing whatever they can to try and get people to work with them again. But people need to remember that the military haven’t actually abided by any of what they have said they will have done over the last five years. They have not met the five-point consensus, and yet people are starting to re-engage with them without having seen any evidence of actual progress.
RFA: The Myanmar military authorities have recently been releasing more information about Daw Aung San Suu Kyi. Do you see this as a reason for optimism? What do you think the Myanmar military’s move might be?
Kim Aris: I always have hope, and I do hope that this will result in actual progress and that she will be free before long. And even before she’s free, I want more regular contact with her, and I want to know that she’s receiving external medical treatment.
RFA: Did they promise you could speak with Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, your mother, regularly?
Kim Aris: No, I haven’t heard anything more on that yet.
RFA: You made it very clear that your mother should never be used as a bargaining chip for diplomatic recognition, sanctions relief, or political advantage. You also urged the UK government and others not to trade humanitarian rights for political legitimacy. And now, one of our RFA audience members raised a difficult question. They asked if negotiation and compromise may be necessary to secure your mother Daw Aung San Suu Kyi’s release. How would you respond to that?
Kim Aris: Well, I realize there are people who have been calling for my mother’s release all the time for the last five years, and without their support, I wouldn’t even have gotten this far. And people do have to negotiate—that’s very clear. At the same time, they should not be legitimizing the military by open discussions like this and welcoming Min Aung Hlaing to their country without actually having secured progress.
RFA: After hearing your mother’s voice for the first time in more than five years, what message would you like to share with the Myanmar people or international community?
Kim Aris: Well, I would say she is sounding well and strong still, but at 81 years old and with ongoing health concerns, and we still don’t know what conditions she’s really been kept under, I’d ask for everybody to continue to fight for her freedom. Burma needs to come forwards, and may may is part of that process still. People need to talk to one another, and one of the few people who is actually able to get people to talk to one another is may may . So please, do not stop fighting for her freedom. Fighting for her freedom is also fighting for the freedom of Burma.
Edited by Charlie Dharapak.

articles.title: Aung San Suu Kyi phone call is ‘political calculation’ by military-backed government
articles.excerpt: Advocates demand full release of Myanmar's former leader after her first contact with family in 5 years.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Burmese
Updated 5:05 PM ET
Allowing Myanmar’s detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi to speak on the phone with her son for the first time in five years is not enough – the military government must immediately release her and all other political prisoners, a human rights advocate told Radio Free Asia Thursday.
The country’s military-backed government announced that the former leader – currently under house arrest – was allowed to talk for 20 minutes to her son Kim Aris at 2:30 p.m. via a call placed to the Myanmar embassy in London, where Aris resides.
The chance to talk to her son came just days after the military released images of her receiving a letter and some books sent by Britain’s King Charles III.
In this image released by the Myanmar government, Aung San Suu Kyi's son, Kim Aris, at the Myanmar embassy in London talks on the phone with his mother, in Naypyidaw, Myanmar, Oct. 22, 2026.
(Myanmar Presidential Spokesman via Reuters) While the phone call was a joyous occasion for mother and son, much more must be done to bring peace to Myanmar, Aung Myo Kyaw, an official with the Thailand-based Assistance Association for Political Prisoners (AAPP), told RFA.
“Aung San Suu Kyi is not only a mother to Kim, but also a mother to the country,” said Aung Myo Kyaw. “What the citizens of the country need is the release of all political prisoners, including Aung San Suu Kyi.”
He said that the gradual easing of restrictions on Aung San Suu Kyi is a political calculation by the military government, which he said was failing in all aspects.
At a time when the military continues to airstrike populated areas of the country, simply allowing her to talk to her son in the U.K. will not bring peace, he said.
“FREE HER. FREE THEM ALL”
In an interview with Radio Free Asia after speaking with his mother, Kim Aris said that it’s clear that the Myanmar military-backed government have been trying to “be more appealing to the international community.”
“But people need to remember that the military haven’t actually abided by any of what they have said they will have done over the last five years,” Aris told RFA. “They have not met the five-point consensus, and yet people are starting to re-engage with them without having seen any evidence of actual progress.”
In a Facebook post, Aris said that he was glad to finally hear his mother’s voice again and thanked supporters for continuing to advocate for her freedom.
But he reiterated that she is still “unjustly detained.”
“One conversation is not regular family access. Family access is not freedom,” he said. “My mother must never be used as a hostage or bargaining chip for diplomatic recognition, sanctions relief or political advantage.”
He called on governments that engage with Myanmar’s military authorities to not legitimize them in exchange for humanitarian rights.
“My mother and all political prisoners must be released immediately and unconditionally. Freedom is not negotiable. Accountability Before Legitimacy. FREE HER. FREE THEM ALL,” he wrote.

Aung San Suu Kyi has been detained since the 2021 military coup that ousted her and the rest of the country’s democratically elected government from power. She was sentenced to 18 years for a broad range of crimes that include corruption and election fraud, though she maintains that she is innocent.
For the duration of her detention, her exact location has not been easy to ascertain, and in April the military government moved her into house arrest . Until the brief phone call with her son Thursday, she had had almost no contact with the outside.
Radio Free Asia attempted to contact a spokesman for the military government to discuss more details about the phone call between Aung San Suu Kyi and Kim Aris, but there was no response.
Updates with Kim Aris comment from RFA interview.
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Pharmacy programme set for launch
articles.excerpt: The Health Bureau today announced that the Community Pharmacy Programme patient pairing arrangement will launch by the end of October. The first phase will be piloted across four districts – Eastern, Yau Tsim Mong, Sha Tin and Yuen Long – with five community pharmacies…
articles.fullText:
The Health Bureau today announced that the Community Pharmacy Programme patient pairing arrangement will launch by the end of October.

The first phase will be piloted across four districts – Eastern, Yau Tsim Mong, Sha Tin and Yuen Long – with five community pharmacies conveniently located near residential areas and shopping malls selected in each district.

Upon successful pairing, participating patients can obtain medications from their preferred pharmacy. Local pharmacists will provide medication counselling and health advice to enhance drug compliance and personal health management.

Drug refill services at these pharmacies will also help prevent excess drug accumulation at home, mitigating the risks of improper storage, misuse and potential wastage. Family doctors participating in the Primary Healthcare Co-care Network will be invited to join the programme in phases. Eligible patients will be invited to enrol, pair with a designated community pharmacy of their choice, and receive briefings on drug dispensing or refill arrangements.

The second phase of the programme will expand to the Southern, Wong Tai Sin, Kwun Tong, Tuen Mun, North and Tai Po districts. The services will be extended to all 18 districts across the city in the fourth quarter of next year, with more eligible pharmacies invited to join thereafter.

Co-payments for Co-care Network participants will follow the Community Drug Formulary, while drug fees for Hospital Authority (HA) patients will remain aligned with the HA's prevailing fee schedule. Furthermore, the annually adjusted consultation co-payment fees for the screening and treatment phases , set by participating family doctors under the established mechanism, will take effect on November 1.

For the treatment phase, 1,022 out of the current 1,239 participating service points will keep their existing co-payment fees unchanged.

Conversely, 28 service points will reduce their fees by a median of $100, while the remaining 189 service points will increase their fees, with nearly 90% of those raising fees by $50 or below. Over 60% of the service points will charge at or below the Government-recommended level of $150.

For the medical screening phase, more than 97% of participating service points will align their fees with the Government-recommended co-payment levels. A small number of clinics will offer rates below the recommended level, including 28 service points for cardiovascular disease risk factor screening and 20 service points for chronic hepatitis B screening.

As of October 7, more than 300,000 citizens have enrolled in the Co-care Network. Among the participants who have completed screening, around 70,000 have been diagnosed with cardiovascular disease risk factors and have entered the treatment phase.

articles.title: Delta region air quality improves
articles.excerpt: A report on the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Pearl River Delta Region’s air quality in 2025 reflects the effectiveness of emission reduction measures in improving air quality across the region. Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macau today jointly released a report on air quality in 2025…
articles.fullText:
A report on the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Pearl River Delta Region’s air quality in 2025 reflects the effectiveness of emission reduction measures in improving air quality across the region.

Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macau today jointly released a report on air quality in 2025 under the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Pearl River Delta Regional Air Quality Monitoring Network.

The report indicates a long-term downward trend in the concentrations of various air pollutants: sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, respirable suspended particulates and fine suspended particulates.

Compared with 20 years ago, the 2025 annual average concentrations for these parameters have declined by between 23% and 86%. Among these, the concentration of fine suspended particulates dropped to 19 μg/m³, reaching a leading national level.

The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government has implemented various emission control measures to enhance air quality.

Moreover, the Air Pollution Control (Amendment) Ordinance 2025 – which came into effect in April last year – updated a number of air quality objectives, with seven out of 15 set at the most stringent levels of the World Health Organization Global Air Quality Guidelines.

The Hong Kong SAR Government is also committed to phasing out approximately 40,000 Euro IV diesel commercial vehicles by the end of 2027. As of August, more than 33,700 such vehicles had been phased out.

To support the green transformation of vehicles to achieve zero vehicular emissions before 2050, Hong Kong will cease new registrations of fuel-propelled private cars, including hybrids, in 2035 or earlier, and will introduce 700 electric buses and 3,000 electric taxis by the end of 2027.

As of the end of September, there were about 185,600 electric vehicles (EVs) in Hong Kong, including about 180,300 electric private cars - approximately six times the 2021 figure and accounting for about 27.6% of all private cars there.

The number of parking spaces with charging facilities in Hong Kong exceeds 170,000, including around 18,090 public chargers. The overall charging infrastructure is sufficient to support more than 290,000 EVs.

articles.fullText:
The Buildings Department approved 10 building plans in August – five on Hong Kong Island, three in Kowloon and two in the New Territories.

Of the approved plans, seven were for apartment and apartment/commercial developments, two were for factory and industrial developments, and one was for community services development.

Consent was given for works on eight building projects. Upon completion, they will provide 70,908 sq m of domestic use involving 1,442 units, and 24,556 sq m of gross floor area for non-domestic use.

Additionally, the department received notification of commencement of superstructure works for six building projects.

It also issued 21 occupation permits, with seven on Hong Kong Island, five in Kowloon and nine in the New Territories.

The buildings certified for occupation comprise 138,920 sq m of domestic gross floor area, involving 1,531 units, and 37,040 sq m for non-domestic use.

Meanwhile, the department also issued seven demolition consents and 487 removal orders, while receiving 3,350 reports about unauthorised building works in August.

articles.title: FS visits Beijing
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan today visited central ministries in Beijing and witnessed the signing of two Memoranda of Understanding on deepening economic and trade co-operations between the Mainland and Hong Kong. In the morning, Mr Chan called on the China Securities…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan today visited central ministries in Beijing and witnessed the signing of two Memoranda of Understanding on deepening economic and trade co-operations between the Mainland and Hong Kong.

In the morning, Mr Chan called on the China Securities Regulatory Commission and met its Chairman Wu Qing. They exchanged views in detail on strengthening collaboration in securities market regulation and development, as well as further deepening mutual market access between the Mainland and Hong Kong.

In the afternoon meeting with Assistant Minister of Commerce Yuan Xiaoming, Mr Chan discussed with Mr Yuan the further deepening of economic and trade co-operation.

Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Algernon Yau, who joined the meeting, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Director-General of the MOC’s Department of Taiwan, Hong Kong & Macao Affairs Sun Yi.

Mr Yau also signed another MOU with Director-General of the MOC’s Department of Pilot Free Trade Zone & Free Trade Port He Yongqian.

The two MOUs were signed in accordance with the mechanism of the Mainland & Hong Kong Economic & Trade Co-operation Committee. Mr Chan and Mr Yuan witnessed the ceremony.

Through the signing of these MOUs, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government and the MOC will further strengthen exchanges and co-operation between the Mainland and Hong Kong in key economic and trade areas, and deepen the alignment of Mainland's pilot free trade zones and free trade port with Hong Kong, respectively.

The MOUs also serve to fully leverage the respective advantages of the two places, jointly serving the country’s high-level opening-up, as well as bringing economic and trade co-operation between the Mainland and Hong Kong to new heights.

Mr Chan thanked the MOC for its continuous strong support for the Hong Kong SAR Government’s efforts to promote Hong Kong’s economic and trade development.

Mr Chan said the Hong Kong SAR Government will leverage the advantages of Hong Kong’s internationalised business environment, professional services system and global resources network, to further give full play to the city’s dual roles as a “super connector" and a ‘super value-adder”.

The Hong Kong SAR Government will also enhance the city’s competitiveness and international influence, consolidate its status as an international trade centre, while contributing to the country’s high-quality economic development, he added.

In the afternoon, Mr Chan also visited an artificial intelligence company and met its senior management.

articles.title: Govt condemns UK report
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today said it strongly condemns the untruthful remarks, slanders and smears contained in the UK's “six-monthly report on Hong Kong: January to June 2026”. In a press statement , the Hong Kong SAR Government rejected the UK's…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today said it strongly condemns the untruthful remarks, slanders and smears contained in the UK's “six-monthly report on Hong Kong: January to June 2026”.

In a press statement , the Hong Kong SAR Government rejected the UK's attempt to interfere in the city’s governance through misleading remarks on local matters.

Emphasising that the core essence of the Sino-British Joint Declaration concerns China's resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong, it said the declaration does not authorise the UK to interfere in Hong Kong's affairs post-handover. The Hong Kong SAR Government urged the UK to respect international law and basic norms governing international relations and immediately cease its long-arm jurisdiction.

The Hong Kong SAR Government reiterated that it steadfastly safeguards the legally protected rights and freedoms enjoyed by Hong Kong people, adding that the city's media landscape has remained vibrant since the implementation of the Hong Kong National Security Law and the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance.

Pointing out the UK's hypocritical double standards, the statement highlighted that the UK had arrested nearly 4,000 people under its own national security and counter-terrorism laws as of June 2026. The statement said it is utterly ugly and despicable that the UK smeared the Hong Kong National Security Law and the city's law enforcement efforts as “undermining rights and freedoms”.

It further stated that the implementation of the Hong Kong National Security Law has brought freedom, stability and improvements to the local business environment, with Hong Kong continuing to be recognised as the world’s freest economy.

Stressing that Hong Kong society is underpinned by the rule of law, the Hong Kong SAR Government said any suggestion that certain individuals or organisations should be immune from consequences for acting illegally runs contrary to the spirit of the rule of law.

Addressing the report's mentions of the judicial verdict against Lai Chee-ying, the Hong Kong SAR Government emphasised that the court's decision was strictly reasoned and well-founded, demonstrating absolute judicial independence.

The reasons for sentence also identified Lai Chee-ying as the mastermind and driving force behind conspiracies of “a grave nature”, noting that Lai Chee-ying opted not to appeal against his conviction or sentence. The statement described it as disgraceful that the UK continues to distort the truth and maliciously attack Hong Kong despite these ironclad facts.

Regarding the mechanism for certificates issued by the Chief Executive under the Hong Kong National Security Law and the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, the Hong Kong SAR Government said that judicial deference to executive authority on national security matters is a general rule practised in regions around the world, including the UK.

articles.title: HK claims 3 silver, 3 bronze
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Culture, Sports & Tourism Rosanna Law today congratulated Hong Kong athletes on winning three silver and three bronze medals at the 5th Asian Para Games across swimming, table tennis and fencing. Swimmer Chan Yui-lam bagged a silver medal in the Women's 200m…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Culture, Sports & Tourism Rosanna Law today congratulated Hong Kong athletes on winning three silver and three bronze medals at the 5th Asian Para Games across swimming, table tennis and fencing.

Swimmer Chan Yui-lam bagged a silver medal in the Women's 200m Individual Medley SM14 event, following her previous success in the butterfly, backstroke, and relay events. Miss Law noted that the results demonstrated Chan Yui-lam’s all-around prowess.

The table tennis team also achieved another milestone, collectively winning two silver and two bronze medals in the doubles events. Chiu Kan-shan and Wong Yue-ching claimed a silver medal in the Women's Doubles - Class WD14 event, while Ng Mui-wui and Wong Ting-ting bagged a silver medal in Women's Doubles - Class WD22 event.

In addition, Ho Ka-sing and Wong Chi-yin earned a bronze medal in the Men's Doubles - Class MD18 event, while Wan Wai-lok and Yuen King-shing claimed a bronze medal in the Men's Doubles - Class MD22 event.

Miss Law said it was a truly gratifying achievement, noting that the table tennis team has now amassed a total of 15 medals – five silver and 10 bronze – in the Asian Para Games.

The sports chief also congratulated fencer Yu Chui-yee on winning a bronze medal in the Women's Sabre Category A event with an outstanding performance.

Tomorrow marks the final day of the Games. Miss Law urged the public to cheer on Hong Kong’s fencing and boccia athletes.

articles.title: Stocks retreat as tech mood sours, oil prices jump
articles.excerpt: Equities sank Thursday as tech firms resumed their downward spiral after a mixed bag of earnings from Wall Street titans, while rising oil prices soured sentiment. AI-linked companies continued the rollercoaster ride they have endured since hitting record highs in June amid…
articles.fullText:
Equities sank Thursday as tech firms resumed their downward spiral after a mixed bag of earnings from Wall Street titans, while rising oil prices soured sentiment.

AI-linked companies continued the rollercoaster ride they have endured since hitting record highs in June amid worries over colossal investment sums and their timeline for profitability, with growing debt-servicing costs adding to the uncertainty.

A blockbuster quarterly report from Elon Musk's SpaceX, its first since listing in June, provided what some hoped would be solid support heading into a crucial earnings season, helping push all three main Wall Street indexes higher Wednesday.

But mixed after-hours releases from Meta and Tesla muddied the waters again for investors.

Tesla announced lower profits in July-September and cut its capital spending forecast for this year, while Facebook-parent Meta lifted its estimates for how much it would spend on artificial intelligence.

Shares of Tesla shed 1.3 percent at the start of trading in New York, while those of Meta slumped 6.7 percent.

"Risk-off sentiment is returning amid high geopolitical tensions and a swirl of worries about financing the AI juggernaut," noted Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.

Wall Street's main indices moved lower, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropping 1.3 percent.

The reports come as traders speculate about the AI boom's outlook, with analysts noting that markets fret when firms ramp up spending but also grow concerned when they pull back.

"Meta's numbers reinforce the AI investment cycle, but funding is becoming an increasingly important part of the conversation," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone.

"Investors will reward growth and monetisation, yet they're also becoming more sensitive to how the next leg of investment is financed and what it means for existing shareholders," he added.

Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet are due to report next week, with Apple and Nvidia up in November.

European stock markets, which feature far fewer major tech firms, were lower in afternoon deals.

The Paris CAC 40 shed 1.0 percent amid concerns over France's high government debt and recent violent street protests across the country.

Barclays dipped 0.5 percent in London after revealing it would cut about 5,000 jobs by year-end as AI increasingly replaces support roles. (AFP)

Edited by Raymond Yeung

articles.title: Evergrande liquidators recover US$435m in asset sales

articles.fullText:
China Evergrande Group's liquidators have recovered US$435.9 million from asset sales and loan recoveries so far, highlighting the challenge of repaying creditors with claims of about US$46 billion against the developer.

In their second progress report since a Hong Kong court ordered Evergrande's liquidation in January 2024, the liquidators, Edward Middleton and Tiffany Wong of Alvarez & Marsal, said on Thursday they aimed to make a first interim dividend payment to creditors in the first half of 2027, although the amount has yet to be determined.

Evergrande, once China's top property developer, defaulted on most of its roughly US$300 billion in liabilities.

The liquidators said they had raised the US$435.9 million through the sale of assets including aircraft, artwork and club memberships, as well as the settlement of loan receivables.

They said 96 of the 107 artworks found at Evergrande's Hong Kong headquarters had been sold for US$28.8 million at a loss. The collection included works by Picasso, Monet and Warhol, as well as sculptures by Moore and Hepworth.

Other assets being sold include a private jet expected to fetch about US$12 million in the fourth quarter. The liquidators are also seeking a US$2 million refund from a US university for part of a donation made in 2020. (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: HSI joins region in retreating amid AI, Hormuz jitters

articles.fullText:
Regional markets retreated as oil prices jumped more than 2 percent following a report by Iran's state television that seven oil tankers caught fire and were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index dived 717 points, or 3.03 percent, to 22,934 on turnover of HK$256.05 billion.

The tech index plunged 200 points, or 5 percent, to 3,793 while the Chia enterprises index fell 254 points, or 3.2 percent, to 7,689.

Dickie Wong, executive director of research at uSmart Securities, said he wasn't bullish in sentiment for the rest of the quarter, given that local stocks fell to a nearly four-month low.

"We are now testing new lows, and probably may test a year-low again – 22,500 points. It may have some kind of rebound, but I don't really see much upside amid concerns about the increasing tension between China and US, and weakening of the Hong Kong dollar," he said.

"Market sentiment is totally changed, especially AI-related and the tech sector facing regulatory pressure. Those negative factors contributed to this market sell-off."

Up north, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index ended down 55 points, or 1.48 percent, at 3,658.

The Shenzhen Component Index dived 347 points, or 2.97 percent, to 11,357 while the ChiNext Index plunged 117 points, or 4.37 percent, to 2,576.

Turnover on the main Shanghai and Shenzhen indices amounted to around 1.53 trillion yuan, up from 1.44 trillion yuan on Wednesday.

If the Iran report is verified, it would be the largest number of vessels damaged in the waterway in a single day since the Iran war started on February 28 in the wake of attacks by US and Israeli forces.

Brent crude, the international standard, gained 3.2 percent to US$112.27 per barrel. It has been bouncing between US$97 and US$112 in recent days on uncertainty about when the war with Iran will allow the global energy industry to return to normal.

US benchmark crude rose 2.8 percent to US$99.80 per barrel.

AI stocks, at the centre of market action in recent months, are under pressure from worries that construction of data centres may slow as it is becoming increasingly expensive to borrow money.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei share average tumbled 1,713 points, or 2.65 percent, to end at 62,907 on heavy selling of big tech companies like SoftBank Group, which lost 6.9 percent. The broader Topix slipped 46 points, or 1.14 percent, to 3,997.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed down 201 points, or 3.52 percent, at 5,533 amid chip-sector profit-taking and the central Bank of Korea's hawkish policy stance on further interest rate hikes. (Additional reporting by agencies)

articles.fullText:
Asian stocks struggled to stay above water in early trade on Thursday, as tech earnings optimism provided only fleeting support amid lingering concerns over artificial intelligence and uncertainty in the Gulf.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened 138 points, or 0.58 percent, down at 23,513 before losses expanded.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index opened up 1 point, at 3,714.

The Shenzhen Component Index opened down 14 points, or 0.12 percent at 11,690. The ChiNext Index fell 6 points, or 0.25 percent, to 2,687.

In the US market, Meta reported third-quarter revenue that beat expectations, while AI server maker Super Micro forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin that both topped estimates.

However, Meta's plan to issue non-voting class C common stock drew renewed scrutiny on AI spending.

"There's a lot of noise out there at the moment and investors are still digesting this morning's results," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

"Also, we're really only at the start of the meaty part of earnings season, which is coming at the same time that investors are tackling the uncertainty from an upcoming Fed decision, geopolitical risks, and US midterms."

In a sign of subdued risk sentiment, the yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes was down 4.2 basis points at 5.1065 percent while the yield on 30-year notes was at a one-week low of 5.3968 percent.

Meanwhile, Brent crude rose 1.1 percent to US$110.03 a barrel, near a five-month high. The United States ordered diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes, while the New York Times reported the US and Israeli militaries had developed specific plans for renewed attacks on Iran after the US midterm elections, which take place on November 3.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 82 points, or 0.13 percent, lower at 64,539 before chip-sector shares gave back the previous session's gains to set the 225 benchmark 680 points back at 63,941 at one stage before noon.

In Seoul, the Kospi opened 65 points, or 1.14 percent, at 5,670 before, like the Nikkei, profit-taking pressure in the chip sector put the benchmark 123 points down at one stage before lunch. (Reuters & Xinhua)
